All 7 active sessions reviewed and cross-referenced against the slots:

**Review conclusions:**
- All three **test-slot holders are live, connected sessions** — leaving test0/1/2 was correct.
- **No stale/disconnected Claude session** exists to reclaim. The only stale holder was the **codex** pool0 (codex sessions don't appear in this Claude-only list — its staleness came from the `~/.codex` rollout check), already released.
- **The contention you're solving:** 6 FamilyFund Claude sessions vs. only 3 test slots. Three FF sessions (#78 seeder, #81 admin email, cross-account) hold no test slot right now — so adding **test3/test4** gives the headroom for them to run isolated suites without waiting. That's consistent with the request.

Everything reconciles. Now to your latest: **vendoring the pool code into ai-harness.**
Now the `link.sh` (mirrors `skills/link.sh`) and a README documenting the code-vs-state split:

Done — the pool code is now vendored in the repo (uncommitted, on this bridge branch):

```
scripts/pool/
├── README.md      code-vs-state split, commands, host-path caveat
├── link.sh        symlinks ~/.familyfund-pool/{pool,testpool}.sh → here (mirrors skills/link.sh)
├── pool.sh        dev/preview pool   (byte-identical to live)
└── testpool.sh    test pool          (live copy, incl. the new test3/test4)
```

Key design point: **only the code is vendored — runtime state (`*.tsv`, `*.lock`, `testdb/`, `warm/`) stays in `~/.familyfund-pool/`**, which the scripts already reference via `$HOME`. So symlinking the code is transparent to every caller (agents + the test-env/lease-env skills).

I deliberately **did not run `link.sh` yet** and left the live `~/.familyfund-pool/*.sh` as untouched real files — nothing is broken. The reason: `link.sh` must point at a **stable checkout**, not this ephemeral `.claude` worktree (a worktree path would dangle when the worktree is GC'd). So full activation needs the files on `main` first.

How far should I take it?
